1.title: Strip both wire ends bare
1.say: Hold one white wire in your left hand. Push its tip into the blue tool, then squeeze to peel off about one centimetre. Do the same with the other white wire.
placements: your first white wire end → with about one centimetre of white cover peeled off to show shiny copper inside (in the video: white wire on right side of blue mat)
your second white wire end → with about one centimetre of white cover peeled off to show shiny copper inside (in the video: white wire on left side of blue mat)
blue peeling tool with red buttons → squeezed around each white wire end near the tip to cut and pull the cover (in the video: held above centre of blue mat)
watch_for: if the copper strands are cut through, you squeezed too deep and need a larger hole
if white cover is still over the tip, you peeled too little and need to peel to about one centimetre
1.check_yourself: It should look like two white wires lying apart with short shiny copper tips showing.
1.safety: Keep your fingers away from the sharp cutting jaws.

2.title: Twist the bare ends together
2.say: Push the copper tips of the two white wires together end to end. Twist them around each other with your fingers until tight.
placements: bare copper ends of the two white wires → pushed together end to end in the middle of the work space and twisted around each other tight by fingers (in the video: bottom centre of blue mat forming one white loop)
watch_for: if the join pulls apart when tugged, it was twisted too loose and needs more twisting
if sharp copper points stick out, they were not twisted flat and will poke through
2.check_yourself: It should look like one white wire loop with a small tight copper twist in the middle.

3.title: Coat the join with paste
3.say: Dip the thin black stick into the cleaning paste called flux. Dab the wet tip all over the copper twist in the middle.
placements: cleaning paste called flux → dabbed to cover all around the twisted copper middle of the white wire loop (in the video: bottom centre of white loop on blue mat)
thin black applicator stick → touched with wet paste tip all over the twisted copper middle (in the video: held from top to bottom centre)
watch_for: if dry copper still shows, you missed a spot and the melted metal will not spread there
if paste is all over the white cover, you used too much and should wipe it clean
3.check_yourself: It should look like the copper twist in the middle of the white loop looks wet and darker.
3.safety: Keep the paste off your skin and eyes.

4.title: Melt metal over the join
4.say: Hold the hot iron tip against the copper twist in the middle. Touch the thin silver wire to the twist, then let it melt and spread.
placements: hot pointed iron tool → point held touching the copper twist in the middle of the white loop (in the video: iron coming from top to bottom centre of blue mat)
thin silver wire → touched to the heated copper twist in the middle until melted silver spreads through and round the back (in the video: fed from right side to bottom centre)
watch_for: if the silver balls up and will not spread, the twist was too cold or had too little paste
if the silver looks dull and lumpy, it moved while cooling and needs reheating until smooth
4.check_yourself: It should look like the middle twist is covered in smooth shiny silver with no copper showing.
4.safety: Do not touch the hot metal tip at any time.

5.title: Slide black tube over join
5.say: Push the short black tube over one white end. Slide it along until it covers the silver middle with white showing both sides.
placements: short black tube → pushed over one white wire end and slid along to the centre to cover the silver middle with white showing both sides (in the video: slid from right end to bottom centre of white loop)
watch_for: if silver still shows at either end, the tube is off centre and needs sliding to cover it
if the tube is loose and slides easily, it is too big and needs a smaller tube
5.check_yourself: It should look like a black tube sitting over the middle with white wire showing on both sides.

6.title: Shrink the tube with heat
6.say: Hold the white wire steady with one hand. Wave the hot air nozzle gently back and forth over the black tube.
placements: hot air nozzle → waved gently back and forth just above the black tube in the middle of the white loop until snug (in the video: silver nozzle from top left over bottom centre of blue mat)
watch_for: if the tube is still loose, you removed the heat too soon and need more gentle heat
if the white cover melts or bubbles, you held the heat too long in one spot
6.check_yourself: It should look like the black tube is tight and snug all around the white wire.
6.safety: Keep the hot air off your skin at all times.
